title: Az Elején, a Végén: Framing the Whole Story

sections.title: A frame around the whole narrative
sections.content: eleje ("the beginning, the front part of something") and vége ("the end of something") behave like hétvége ("weekend") — you already reach for the superessive with hétvégén ("on the weekend"); the exact same suffix gives you elején ("at the beginning") and végén ("at the end"). Put the story in front of them — a történet elején, a történet végén — and you have a frame for the whole narrative, separate from the előbb/aztán/végül chain you use to sequence what happens inside it.

sections.title: Framing a story
rows: at the beginning of the story
at the end of the story
At the beginning..., but in the end...

items.spanish: A történet elején Meg és Károly Bécsbe utaztak.
items.english: At the beginning of the story, Meg and Károly traveled to Vienna.

items.spanish: Az elején esett az eső, de a végén gyönyörű volt az idő.
items.english: At the beginning it was raining, but in the end the weather was gorgeous.

items.spanish: A történet végén mindenki nagyot nevetett.
items.english: At the end of the story, everyone laughed heartily.

sections.content: elején/végén frame the WHOLE story, like a frame around a picture; előbb/aztán/utána/később/végül sequence the events INSIDE it. Good storytelling uses both together, not one instead of the other.
